split_policy: Original acquisition-group splits and four scan exclusions. No test tuning. All complete training cells each epoch. Unknown unmarked cells not global negative examples.
selection: Validation mean symmetric boundary error on fixed production-box matches; retain all failures in paired scores using original masks. Require >=99% original matches still IoU>=0.5 and non-increasing volume MAPE. Reject expansions without membrane evidence or into neighbors. No selection by test metrics.
test: Freeze final validation choice before test comparison. Fixed baseline cell identities and original signal centers. Physical closed-mesh volumes, symmetric surface distances and A-to-surface distances; lost points and failures reported, all outliers included. Historically reused test split remains exploratory.
deployment: Preserve current defaults while experimenting. Save candidates and diagnostics separately. Adopt only with demonstrated validation benefit and passing integration checks; no release requested.
production_crop_addendum: Following completed crop diagnostics, retraining uses frozen matched predicted boxes/seeds for marked training cells. Unmatched complete training cells remain in manual crops. All 1493 training cells retained. Validation checkpoint physical boundary score uses only the fixed baseline 441 matches, with all 574 validation targets still evaluated for loss. No test targets in patches.
residual_loss_control_addendum: Registered during residual asymmetric-loss training, before any test evaluation: repeat residual architecture with balanced beta=0.5 on the same surface-loss parent to separate architecture effects from the unsuccessful beta=0.6 penalty. Same epochs/patience/data and validation selection rules.
final_calibration_addendum: Before any test evaluation, recalibrate only the final selected network on the original registered cutoff grid and fixed validation identities. Same surface/volume/match guards. Training may change probability calibration. No new grid values or test-guided parameters.
